steps.note: Cleanup1: 140Ce- (real cells; bead channel empty). Bead: 140Ce++ (calibration beads labeled with cerium).

Cleanup2: Residual mid-range. Residual is a CyTOF Helios Gaussian-discrimination parameter (ion-cloud fit residual), NOT a biological marker. Mid-range = clean singlet event; extreme values indicate doublets, partial events, or acquisition artifacts.

Cleanup3: Center mid-to-high. Center is a CyTOF Helios Gaussian-discrimination parameter (ion-cloud centroid), NOT a biological marker. Properly-centered events correspond to well-formed droplets with intact ion clouds.

Cleanup4: Offset mid-range. Offset is a CyTOF Helios Gaussian-discrimination parameter (baseline offset of the ion-cloud signal), NOT a biological marker. Mid-range = normal event baseline; extreme values flag acquisition artifacts.

Cleanup5: Width mid-range. Width is a CyTOF Helios Gaussian-discrimination parameter (ion-cloud temporal width), NOT a biological marker. Typical width = singlet event; wider signals indicate doublets or aggregates.
Cleanup6: 103Rh- (Rhodium viability dye excluded from live cells; dead cells are Rh+).
Ir: 191Ir_DNA1++ (Iridium-191 intercalator marks nucleated real cells).
CD45: CD45+ (leukocyte common antigen; all white blood cells). Doublet/debris exclusion handled upstream.

Mononuclear: CD45+ CD66b- (lymphocytes, monocytes, DCs). Granulocyte: CD45int CD66b+ (granulocytes express CD66b with intermediate CD45). CD66bnegCD45lo: CD45lo CD66b- (dying cells / debris). CD45hiCD66bpos: CD45hi CD66b+ (atypical — activated granulocytes or contamination). Useful co-markers: CD16 confirms Granulocyte (neutrophils CD16+); CD3/CD19 low confirms Mononuclear.

CD14negCD56neg: CD14- CD56- (excludes monocytes and NK cells from the mononuclear fraction). Useful co-markers: CD16 helps flag residual NK contamination (NK are CD56+ CD16+); CD3/CD19 low confirms no T/B carryover.

CD123negCD3neg: CD3- CD123lo/- (excludes T cells and CD123-high basophils/pDCs; retains B and other residual lineages). Useful co-markers: HLA-DR helps sanity-check the CD123 split — CD123+ basophils are HLA-DR-, while CD123+ pDCs are HLA-DR+ (both would be excluded by this gate, but HLA-DR confirms which is which).
CD20neg: CD20- (any CD19) — includes both CD19-CD20- background and CD19+CD20- plasmablasts (plasmablasts separated at Step14). TotalCD19B: CD19+ CD20+ (main mature B cell pool).

NaiveB: IgD+ CD27- (un-activated naive B cells, no class switch). IgDnegMemB: IgD- CD27+ (class-switched memory B cells). IgDposMemB: IgD+ CD27+ (non-switched / IgM memory B cells). Useful co-markers: CD38 high may flag plasmablast-adjacent cells (but true plasmablasts are gated separately at Step14 from the CD20- branch).

Plasmablast: CD27++ CD38++ (antibody-secreting B-lineage cells; rare population, typically <5% of parent). Useful co-markers: CD19+ is required — parent (CD20-) includes CD19+CD20- plasmablasts and CD19-CD20- background; only CD19+ cells with CD27++CD38++ are true plasmablasts.

NonTNonB: CD19- CD3- (excludes B and T cells from the mononuclear fraction). Useful co-markers: CD14 — the Mononuclear parent still includes monocytes, so some CD14+ cells spill into NonTNonB; they are removed downstream at Step17/21.
NonBNonNK: CD56- CD20- (further cleanup to exclude NK cells and any residual B cells).
TotalMonocyte: CD14+ (monocytes; all monocyte subsets are CD14+). Useful co-markers: HLA-DR+ confirms monocyte identity (monocytes are HLA-DR+; absence suggests residual debris or contamination).

Blood monocytes are classically split into three subsets: classical (most abundant, inflammatory), intermediate, and non-classical (patrolling). The canonical scheme uses CD14 × CD16 (classical = CD14++ CD16-, non-classical = CD14dim CD16+). This panel replaces CD16 with CD38 — classical monocytes are metabolically most active (CD38-high), while non-classical are CD38-low after further differentiation. ClassicalMono: CD14++ CD38+ (most abundant, inflammatory). TransitionalMono: CD14int CD38int (intermediate differentiation). NonclassicalMono: CD14+ CD38- (parent is CD14+; distinguished from classical by CD38 loss). Useful co-markers: CD16 — not used by this gate, but canonical non-classical monocytes are CD16+; CD16 level is a useful sanity check against the CD38-based split.

Basophil: HLA-DR- CD123++ (basophils, IL-3Rα-high, lack HLA-DR). HLADRloCD123lo: HLA-DR- CD123- (residual population; may contain ILCs). Useful co-markers: CD16 is classical for distinguishing basophils (CD16-) from residual neutrophils (CD16+); confirms Basophil vs granulocyte spillover.
ILC: CD127+ CD161+ (innate lymphoid cells; IL-7Rα+ and CD161+).
NonTNonBCD14neg: CD3- CD14- (further cleanup of NonTNonB; enriches for NK cells and DCs).

TotalDC: HLA-DR+ CD56- (dendritic cells; HLA-DR-high, no CD56). TotalNK: CD56+ HLA-DR- (NK cells; CD56+ without HLA-DR). Useful co-markers: CD11c/CD123 distinguish DC subtypes downstream (Step24); CD3 low confirms no T-cell contamination; CD14 low confirms no monocyte spillover.

EarlyNK: CD56+ CD57- (immature NK, corresponds to CD56bright / cytokine-producing). LateNK: CD56+ CD57+ (mature cytotoxic NK, terminally differentiated). Useful co-markers: CD16 marks the main cytotoxic NK compartment (CD56dim CD16+); combined with CD57 confirms mature cytotoxic NK (LateNK).

pDC: CD123+ CD11c- (plasmacytoid DC; IL-3Rα+, lacks integrin αX). cDC: CD11c+ CD123- (conventional / classical DC). Useful co-markers: HLA-DR should be high for both pDC and cDC (DC hallmark); CD14 low excludes monocyte spillover.
mDC: CD123- CD38+ (myeloid DCs within the conventional DC compartment).
CD11cnegCD14neg: CD11c- CD14- (non-myeloid residual within the mononuclear fraction).
CD3T: CD3+ CD19- (T cells).
abT: CD3+ TCRgd- (αβ T cells, the majority of CD3+ cells). gdT: CD3+ TCRgd+ (γδ T cells, minority).

CD8: CD4- CD8+ (cytotoxic T cells). CD4: CD4+ CD8- (helper T cells). DPT: CD4+ CD8+ (double-positive; rare, often thymic emigrants or activated transitional). DNT: CD4- CD8- (double-negative; includes NKT and MAIT precursors). Useful co-markers: CD161 — DNT is enriched for MAIT/NKT (resolved later at Step61); high CD161 on DNT cells flags these unconventional T cells.

CD8Naive: CD45RA+ CD27+ (naive CD8). CD8TEMRA: CD45RA+ CD27- (terminally differentiated effector memory re-expressing CD45RA). CD8/CD45RAnegCD27pos: CD45RA- CD27+ (central memory / early effector memory). CD8/CD45RAnegCD27neg: CD45RA- CD27- (late effector memory). Useful co-markers: CD45RO complements CD45RA (memory cells are CD45RO+ CD45RA-; naive are CD45RO- CD45RA+); CD28 helps distinguish less-differentiated (CD28+) vs late (CD28-) memory.

HLA-DR marks activation (MHC-II induced on recently-activated T cells). CD38 marks proliferation / metabolic activity. CD8Naive/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38- (activated, not proliferating). CD8Naive/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+ (proliferating, not classically activated — e.g. recent thymic emigrants). CD8Naive/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+ (dually activated and proliferating).

CD8TCM: CCR7+ (central memory; lymph-node homing retained). CD8TEM1: CCR7- (effector memory with CD27 retained — earliest EM stage in this panel's progression). Useful co-markers: CD28 retained in TCM and early EM, lost in late EM; CD45RO confirms memory status (CD45RO+).
HLA-DR = activation; CD38 = proliferation. CD8TEM1/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38-. CD8TEM1/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+. CD8TEM1/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+.
HLA-DR = activation; CD38 = proliferation. CD8TCM/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38-. CD8TCM/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+. CD8TCM/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+.

CD8TEM2: CCR7+ (intermediate differentiation; CD27 lost but CCR7 retained). CD8TEM3: CCR7- (terminally differentiated effector memory; both CD27 and CCR7 lost). Useful co-markers: CD28 — early EM (TEM1) often retains CD28; progressive loss from TEM2 → TEM3 toward terminal differentiation. CD45RO+ confirms memory status.
HLA-DR = activation; CD38 = proliferation. CD8TEM3/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38-. CD8TEM3/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+. CD8TEM3/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+.
HLA-DR = activation; CD38 = proliferation. CD8TEM2/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38-. CD8TEM2/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+. CD8TEM2/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+.
HLA-DR = activation; CD38 = proliferation. CD8TEMRA/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38-. CD8TEMRA/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+. CD8TEMRA/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+.
Aggregated activation status across all non-naive CD8. HLA-DR = activation; CD38 = proliferation. nnCD8/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38-. nnCD8/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+. nnCD8/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+.

CD4Naive: CD45RA+ CD27+ (naive CD4). CD4TEMRA: CD45RA+ CD27- (terminally differentiated effector memory re-expressing CD45RA; rare in CD4). CD4/CD45RAnegCD27pos: CD45RA- CD27+ (central memory / early EM). CD4/CD45RAnegCD27neg: CD45RA- CD27- (late effector memory).
HLA-DR = activation; CD38 = proliferation. CD4Naive/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38-. CD4Naive/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+. CD4Naive/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+.

CD4TCM: CCR7+ (central memory; lymph-node homing retained). CD4TEM1: CCR7- (early effector memory with CD27 retained). Useful co-markers: CD28 retained in TCM, progressively lost toward late EM; CD45RO confirms memory status.
HLA-DR = activation; CD38 = proliferation. CD4TEM1/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38-. CD4TEM1/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+. CD4TEM1/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+.
HLA-DR = activation; CD38 = proliferation. CD4TCM/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38-. CD4TCM/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+. CD4TCM/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+.

CD4TEM2: CCR7+ (intermediate differentiation; CD27 lost but CCR7 retained). CD4TEM3: CCR7- (terminally differentiated effector memory; both CD27 and CCR7 lost). Useful co-markers: CD28 — early EM often retains CD28; progressive loss from TEM2 → TEM3 toward terminal differentiation. CD45RO+ confirms memory CD4.
HLA-DR = activation; CD38 = proliferation. CD4TEM2/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38-. CD4TEM2/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+. CD4TEM2/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+.
HLA-DR = activation; CD38 = proliferation. CD4TEM3/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38-. CD4TEM3/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+. CD4TEM3/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+.
HLA-DR = activation; CD38 = proliferation. CD4TEMRA/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38-. CD4TEMRA/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+. CD4TEMRA/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+.
Aggregated activation status across all non-naive CD4. HLA-DR = activation; CD38 = proliferation. nnCD4/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38-. nnCD4/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+. nnCD4/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+.

CXCR5 is a B-cell follicle homing receptor; CXCR5+ CD4 cells include T follicular helper (Tfh). nnCD4CXCR5pos: CXCR5+ (Tfh and Tfh-like). nnCD4CXCR5neg: CXCR5- (non-Tfh non-naive CD4). Useful co-markers: CD45RO+ confirms memory CD4 (Tfh are antigen-experienced); PD-1/ICOS are gold-standard Tfh markers but not in this panel.
HLA-DR = activation; CD38 = proliferation. nnCD4CXCR5pos/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38-. nnCD4CXCR5pos/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+. nnCD4CXCR5pos/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+.

Treg: CD25+ CD127-/lo (regulatory T cells; IL-2Rα-high, IL-7Rα-low — classical Treg signature). Scope caveat: this gate is applied on non-naive CD4 only (parent excludes CD4Naive). It therefore captures memory/effector Treg (Miyara Fraction II/III). Resting CD45RA+ Treg (Miyara Fraction I) are NOT captured here — they fall into CD4Naive by this panel's design. Useful co-markers: CD45RA distinguishes resting (CD45RA+) vs activated/memory (CD45RA-) Treg; lack of HLA-DR at baseline supports Treg vs contaminating activated CD4.
HLA-DR = activation; CD38 = proliferation. Treg/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38-. Treg/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+. Treg/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+.

Chemokine receptor panel for Th polarization. Th1: CXCR3+ CCR6- (IFNγ producers). Th17: CXCR3- CCR6+ (IL-17 producers; note: CCR6+ alone may include Th22-like cells — CCR4 co-expression refines classical Th17). NonTh1NonTh17: CXCR3- CCR6- (candidate Th2, Th9, or uncommitted effectors — Th2 is resolved at Step57 by CCR4). Useful co-markers: CD45RO+ confirms memory CD4 (Th polarization occurs in the memory compartment); CCR4 further discriminates classical Th17 (CCR6+ CCR4+) from Th22-like (CCR6+ CCR4-, CCR10 not in panel); CD294 (CRTH2) resolves Th2 at the next step.
HLA-DR = activation; CD38 = proliferation. Th1/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38-. Th1/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+. Th1/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+.
HLA-DR = activation; CD38 = proliferation. Th17/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38-. Th17/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+. Th17/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+.

Th2: CXCR3- CCR4+ (Th2 express CCR4 and CRTH2; lack CXCR3). CCR4+ is also expressed on Th17, but CCR6+ Th17 were already gated out upstream (Step54 NonTh1NonTh17), so CCR4+ here specifically marks Th2. Useful co-markers: CD294 (CRTH2) is the gold-standard Th2 marker and is available in this panel — CRTH2+ strongly confirms Th2 identity.
HLA-DR = activation; CD38 = proliferation. Th2/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38-. Th2/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+. Th2/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+.
HLA-DR = activation; CD38 = proliferation. DNT/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38-. DNT/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+. DNT/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+.
HLA-DR = activation; CD38 = proliferation. DPT/activated: HLA-DR+ CD38-. DPT/CD38pos: HLA-DR- CD38+. DPT/activated+CD38pos: HLA-DR+ CD38+.

MAITNKT: CD161++ AND CD4- within αβT. This gate captures both MAIT and invariant NKT cells based on high CD161 combined with the CD4-negative constraint. The CD4 axis is displayed to reveal the CD4 vs non-CD4 split: MAIT cells are predominantly CD8+ or double-negative (CD4-), while invariant NKT cells are more often CD4+ or double-negative. Useful co-markers: CD56 co-expression biases toward NKT; Vα7.2 TCR is MAIT gold-standard but not in this panel; TCRgd exclusion is already enforced by the αβT parent.

Neutrophil: CD16+ CD294- (mature neutrophils; FcγRIII+). Eosinophil: CD16- CD294+ (CRTH2+ eosinophils). Useful co-markers: HLA-DR low confirms granulocyte identity for both subsets (basophil contamination would show HLA-DR- CD123+, but basophils are excluded by the Granulocyte parent already).
